rules.sentence: This case illustrates the very frequent occurrence of the metabolic syndrome and development of type 2 diabetes, even with only minimal weight gain in women with Turner syndrome.
Adequate hormone replacement has been shown likely to reduce the risk of developing diabetes.

The increased morbidity and mortality associated with cardiovascular and cerebrovascular disease in Turner syndrome is likely multifactorial, and therefore it is very important to pay careful attention to vascular risk factors during clinic review, including BP control, metabolic factors such as diabetes mellitus, hyperlipidemia, and MASLD, as well as advocating healthy lifestyle with weight management, exercise, and avoidance of smoking.
At the age of 51 years, she developed type 2 diabetes (no positive autoantibodies for type 1 diabetes).
